summary: Well-executed, fully artifacted confirmatory study with comprehensive deterministic logging and hashes. The autonomous pipeline, preregistration, execution manifest, and deterministic artifacts are strong. However the manuscript fails to record a clear preregistration deviation: the preregistered primary estimand (difference in AUC-ROC between composite and best submetric) could not be evaluated because the test set contained no positive outage labels, yet the analysis/deviation record does not explicitly document that the AUC comparison was unexecuted. The authors must (a) explicitly disclose and document that the primary AUC estimand was uncomputable and mark this as a formal deviation from the preregistration, and (b) provide the trained composite-model coefficients or an artifact-level explanation showing the composite training and application pipeline and where those artifacts live. After these required, artifact-resolvable clarifications the paper will be acceptable.
critical_issues: The preregistered primary estimand (difference in AUC-ROC: composite vs best single submetric) was not evaluated because the held-out test set contained zero positive outage labels; this preregistration deviation is not recorded in the analysis/deviations_from_preregistration record (analysis_results.deviations_from_preregistration is empty). The manuscript therefore lacks an explicit, machine-readable deviation declaration tying the unexecuted AUC comparison to the observed all-success outcome.

The manuscript asserts that a penalized logistic-regression composite was trained on train+val and applied to test, but the trained-model coefficients/serialization and training diagnostics (hyperparameter selection, regularization weight, validation performance) are not referenced as artifacts/hashes. Without those artifacts it is impossible to verify that the composite was produced as preregistered and how it was applied to the test set.

The paper’s confirmatory framing emphasizes the preregistered AUC-based comparison; reporting a paired binary success-rate analysis as the primary statistical result (McNemar/bootstrap on 200/200 successes) constitutes a substantive analysis-shift that must be documented formally in the preregistration-deviation log and in a clear ‘Preregistration fidelity’ subsection in the manuscript.
required_revisions: Add an explicit, machine-readable preregistration-deviation record (and include its path and SHA-256 in the evidence bundle) that (a) names the preregistered primary estimand (AUC-ROC composite vs best submetric), (b) states it was uncomputable on the held-out test because there were zero positive outage labels, (c) cites the specific artifact(s) proving the zero-positive-label distribution (e.g., analysis/condition_summary.csv and paired_contingency_table.csv with SHA-256), and (d) explains that the reported paired binary success-rate analysis is an observational/alternative outcome arising from the ceiling effect. This must be added to analysis/deviations_from_preregistration and summarized in the manuscript (e.g., a short Preregistration Fidelity subsection). All changes must reference existing artifacts and their hashes.

Publish the trained composite-model artifact(s) (penalized logistic regression coefficients, hyperparameter setting, training/validation diagnostics) and their file path(s) and SHA-256(s) in the evidence bundle, or if such artifacts were not produced, add an explicit artifact-level statement (with SHA) that composite training output was not materialized and explain why (and how the composite score was computed/applied). The manuscript must cite the artifact path/sha where the composite weights and scoring code live (or the absence thereof).

Add a concise table or paragraph in the manuscript enumerating each preregistered estimand/analysis step (primary, secondary, exploratory) and annotate for each: (executed / unexecuted / modified), with short justification and artifact references (paths + SHA-256). Ensure the analysis_results.deviations_from_preregistration field (and related logs) reflect this information so reviewers and readers can verify the exact preregistration fidelity from provided artifacts.
optional_revisions: In Results or Methods add the concrete composite-score distribution (summary statistics) on train/val and test (even if non-discriminative) with artifact references so readers can inspect score spread despite label degeneracy.

Expand the Discussion slightly to enumerate concrete, reproducible strategies for generating failure-rich synthetic tasks (adversarial perturbations, calibrated emulator noise, injected parser faults) and point to which artifacts in the bundle could be adapted to produce such follow-on experiments.

Include a short appendix-like snippet (within the 5-page limit) listing the exact paths and SHA-256 hashes for: (a) trained-composite artifact, (b) composite-scoring code, (c) ROC/AUPRC routine that was planned but omitted—this will improve transparency and reproducibility even though the discriminative plots were degenerate.
